audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says Flux chains 'require melee contact'. Ryze has no melee requirement. Short Fuse was never mentioned.
audit.why: Spell Flux is a 615-range cast and Rune Prison is 615; Overload reaches 1000. Ziggs' Bouncing Bomb is 850 and Hexplosive Minefield 900. The real problem is a 235-unit gap between where he can hit you and where you can start a chain — a precise, checkable number instead of a wrong category. Short Fuse is an auto-attack reset whose cooldown shortens every time he casts, so his burst opens on an attack wind-up.
audit.corrected: Every 'melee contact' line replaced with the 615-vs-850 range gap; Short Fuse's auto-reset tell written into the Don'ts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge was the tracked spike in six places with no cooldown, and the page never mentions it knocks Ziggs away too.
audit.why: 20/18/16/14/12s — 20 seconds at rank 1. Riot's text: 'Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage', which is why it is simultaneously his interrupt and his escape, and why its downtime is the only window you get.
audit.corrected: 20 seconds at rank 1 and the self-knockback written into the phases, the Do's and the foe wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 were 'Skill' in both layers while their own whys describe Ziggs adding an interrupt at 2 and denying you any chain at 3; the 2+ item row gave Ryze the win while its why calls the two of you even.
audit.why: Ziggs owns the first three levels outright on range, the middle is a managed grind, first item is your window, and full build is even. The packet chart states that and 51.28% fits it.
audit.corrected: Ziggs, Ziggs, Ziggs, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Skill — paired full/content rows with ratings.

edits.before: W root threatens jungle follow-up, but it's also your kite tool — spending it greedily is how you die.
edits.after: Satchel Charge knocks you out of your W window every 20s at rank 1 — that is his real interrupt.

edits.before: Full kit: E-Flux into W root into Q chain is your trade. Fluxed minions make the wave itself your weapon.
edits.after: Your Flux reaches 615 while Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 — he never grants you the 235 in between.

edits.before: Seraph's online — you out-DPS and out-tank everyone in extended fights. Side-lane and Warp to every fight.
edits.after: Seraph's is online, but Mega Inferno Bomb still zones objectives from 5000 — win fights, not sieges.

edits.before: His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Satchel Charge knocks him away too, and returns every 20s at rank 1 — he is catchable only in that gap.

edits.before: Ziggs spends Satchel Charge early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Ziggs spends Satchel Charge on the wave — the next 20 seconds at rank 1 are yours.

edits.before: That’s Ziggs’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Short Fuse resets his auto — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast bar.

edits.before: Your full E-Q-W loop is live but he is still three Bouncing Bomb lengths away — Flux chains require melee contact he never gives you voluntarily.
edits.after: Your full E-Q-W loop is live but Spell Flux only reaches 615 while Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 — he never volunteers the 235 units in between.

edits.before: Ziggs's Bouncing Bomb (Q) and Hexplosive Minefield (E) deny you the melee range you need to Flux-stack — you cannot run a single E-Q-W rotation without eating half your HP bar.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 and Hexplosive Minefield covers 900 while your Spell Flux needs 615 — you cannot run one E-Q-W rotation without eating half your HP bar getting there.

edits.before: Satchel Charge (W) is Ziggs's panic button and positioning tool — if he knocks you away mid-combo your W root whiffs and the trade collapses.
edits.after: Satchel Charge (W) is his panic button and it knocks him away too, on 20s at rank 1 — if it lands mid-combo your root whiffs and the trade collapses.

edits.before: Keep you at max Bouncing Bomb (Q) range to prevent the melee contact needed to apply Spell Flux (E)
edits.after: Hold you outside Bouncing Bomb's 850 so you never reach the 615 where Spell Flux starts a chain

edits.before: Use Satchel Charge (W) to knock you away the instant your W root animation begins
edits.after: Use Satchel Charge to knock you away the instant Rune Prison lands, once every 20s

edits.before: Ziggs completely out-ranges you at levels 1 through 3 — his Bouncing Bomb (Q) reaches you before you can walk into E range, and his Hexplosive Minefield (E) punishes every step forward. Do not attempt your E-Q-W combo unless he has physically walked up; he almost never will. Stack Manaflow Band passively, last-hit with Q at its maximum reach, and accept that you are not trading here — you are surviving. The wave being pushed toward you is actually fine: it shortens his bomb arc and lets you CS under tower.
edits.after: Ziggs out-ranges you at levels 1 through 3 — Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 and Hexplosive Minefield covers 900, while Spell Flux needs 615, so every step toward a chain costs health. Do not attempt the E-Q-W combo unless he has walked up; he almost never will. Stack Manaflow Band passively, last-hit with Overload at its full 1000, and accept that you are surviving, not trading. The wave pushed toward you is fine: it shortens his bomb arc and lets you CS under tower.

notes: The kit's derived flags tag Satchel Charge with percentHealth. Riot's own description says nothing about percent-health damage — the flag most likely picked up the turret 'hexplode' clause — so per the brief's rule the description was trusted and no percent-health claim was written. Everything about Satchel Charge on the page is now its knock-back, its self-knockback, and its 20-second rank-1 cooldown, all of which are stated in the text.
